system_design.name: Design a Notification System
system_design.prompt: Design a multi-channel notification platform that can deliver push, email, and SMS notifications for many product teams.
clarification_questions: Which channels and notification types are in scope?
What traffic volume and delivery-latency target should we design for?
What delivery guarantee is required?
How should user preferences and opt-outs behave?
How should priorities and provider outages be handled?

hidden_constraints.delivery: at-least-once internally; provider APIs are ambiguous on timeout

system_design.exercise: Run a 45-minute mock interview without consulting a solution.
system_design.hermes_connection: Use scheduled Telegram delivery only as experience to reason from, not as the answer.
reference_solution: Separate ingestion, preference filtering, scheduling, channel queues, workers, and delivery status.
Use a durable notification record plus per-channel attempts and idempotency keys.
Isolate providers with rate limiters, exponential backoff, circuit breakers, and dead-letter handling.
Partition queues by channel and priority; scale workers on age and depth, not only CPU.
Track accepted, attempted, provider-acknowledged, failed, and user-visible outcomes separately.

system_design.name: Design a Distributed Rate Limiter
system_design.prompt: Design a distributed rate-limiting service used by thousands of backend services.
clarification_questions: What identities and policies can be limited?
How accurate must enforcement be?
What latency and availability are required?
Are limits global or regional?

hidden_constraints.availability: prefer bounded over-admission to global outage

system_design.exercise: Run a 45-minute mock interview without consulting a solution.
system_design.hermes_connection: Compare API admission control with Telegram provider rate limits.
reference_solution: Keep policy configuration separate from the hot enforcement path.
Use token buckets with atomic updates in regional in-memory stores.
Shard by limiter key and use local leases for very hot global limits.
Define explicit fail-open or fail-closed behavior by endpoint risk.
Observe denied traffic, store latency, skew, and estimated over-admission.

system_design.name: Design a Distributed Task Queue
system_design.prompt: Design a distributed task queue for background jobs with delays, priorities, retries, and worker crashes.
clarification_questions: What task sizes and throughput are expected?
What delivery semantics are required?
Are ordering and scheduling needed?
How long may tasks run?
How should poison tasks be handled?
system_design.exercise: Run a 45-minute mock interview without consulting a solution.
system_design.hermes_connection: Reason from long-running Hermes jobs and retries, while designing for multi-tenant scale.
reference_solution: Persist task metadata and payload references before acknowledging enqueue.
Workers claim visibility leases and heartbeat long tasks; expired leases make work eligible again.
Require idempotent handlers because exactly-once execution is not guaranteed.
Use partitioned ready queues plus a delayed-task index and promotion workers.
Bound retries and route poison tasks to a dead-letter workflow with tenant quotas.

system_design.name: Design a Webhook Delivery Platform
system_design.prompt: Design a multi-tenant webhook delivery platform for external customer endpoints.
clarification_questions: What ordering and delivery guarantees matter?
What volume and payload sizes are expected?
How are endpoints authenticated?
How long should retries continue?
What customer controls and visibility are needed?

hidden_constraints.tenancy: one slow customer must not affect others

system_design.exercise: Run a 45-minute mock interview without consulting a solution.
system_design.hermes_connection: Compare outbound webhook uncertainty with bot-provider delivery uncertainty.
reference_solution: Write events to an outbox, fan out durable delivery attempts, and sign each request.
Partition by tenant or endpoint while bounding per-destination concurrency.
Resolve and validate destinations against SSRF policy before controlled egress.
Retry transient failures with jitter and endpoint-aware circuit breakers.
Expose attempt histories, replay controls, lag, and terminal failure reasons.

system_design.name: Design a Global Job Scheduler
system_design.prompt: Design a global scheduler for recurring and one-time jobs across multiple regions.
clarification_questions: What scheduling precision is needed?
How many jobs and executions are expected?
Can jobs overlap?
What happens during regional failover?
How are time zones and daylight-saving changes handled?

hidden_constraints.failover: no silent loss; rare duplicate dispatch is acceptable

system_design.exercise: Run a 45-minute mock interview without consulting a solution.
system_design.hermes_connection: Use the existing OS cron separation as a small-system baseline.
reference_solution: Store canonical schedules separately from materialized upcoming executions.
Partition time buckets and lease scheduler ownership with fencing tokens.
Publish due executions durably and make downstream work idempotent.
Define DST, missed-run, overlap, and catch-up policies explicitly.
Measure scheduling delay, duplicate rate, missed runs, and partition ownership health.

system_design.name: Design a Global Messaging System
system_design.prompt: Design a globally distributed messaging system for one-to-one and group conversations.
clarification_questions: Which messaging features are required?
What ordering guarantee is expected?
How large can groups become?
What offline and multi-device behavior is required?
What privacy constraints apply?
system_design.exercise: Run a 45-minute mock interview without consulting a solution.
system_design.hermes_connection: Contrast a global service with the current single-user Telegram workflows.
reference_solution: Assign conversation sequence numbers within a partition rather than claim global ordering.
Persist messages before asynchronous delivery and track per-user cursors.
Use fanout-on-write for ordinary groups and hybrid fanout for huge groups.
Place conversation ownership near active users and replicate with explicit failover semantics.
Separate message durability, delivery, read state, presence, and push notification paths.

system_design.name: Design a Video Recommendation System
system_design.prompt: Design the personalized home-page recommendation system for a large video platform.
clarification_questions: What user outcome should be optimized?
What surfaces and freshness are in scope?
What traffic and catalog size are expected?
What safety or diversity constraints matter?
How quickly must new users and videos be served?
system_design.exercise: Run a 45-minute mock interview without consulting a solution.
system_design.hermes_connection: Relate adaptive study selection to ranking objectives without equating the scales.
reference_solution: Define a multi-objective target with satisfaction and safety guardrails, not watch time alone.
Generate candidates from retrieval, subscriptions, trends, and exploration, then rank in stages.
Use point-in-time-correct training data and distinguish batch from real-time features.
Evaluate offline ranking quality and calibration before guarded online experiments.
Monitor freshness, drift, subgroup outcomes, feedback loops, and serving degradation.

system_design.name: Design a Real-Time Fraud Detection System
system_design.prompt: Design a real-time fraud detection system for card transactions.
clarification_questions: What action can the model take?
What latency and transaction volume are required?
How are fraud labels obtained and delayed?
What false-positive cost is acceptable?
How should rules and human review interact with the model?
system_design.exercise: Run a 45-minute mock interview without consulting a solution.
system_design.hermes_connection: Use explicit evidence and auditability principles from local study tracking.
reference_solution: Separate risk scoring from the approve, decline, and review decision policy.
Combine low-latency aggregates, identity/device signals, graph features, rules, and a calibrated model.
Train with point-in-time joins and account for delayed, biased labels.
Measure expected cost, recall at review capacity, calibration, and subgroup behavior.
Monitor feature freshness, approval shifts, review outcomes, drift, and adversarial adaptation.

system_design.name: Design an Enterprise RAG System
system_design.prompt: Design an enterprise question-answering system over private documents using retrieval-augmented generation.
clarification_questions: Which sources and content types are in scope?
How fresh must answers be?
How are document permissions enforced?
What answer quality and citation requirements apply?
What latency and cost targets matter?
system_design.exercise: Run a 45-minute mock interview without consulting a solution.
system_design.hermes_connection: Compare with retrieval over local paper and interview history.
reference_solution: Build incremental ingestion with parsing, deduplication, chunking, metadata, embeddings, and ACL propagation.
Use tenant-aware hybrid retrieval, filtering, reranking, and explicit context budgets.
Generate answers with citations and abstain when evidence is insufficient.
Evaluate retrieval and answer quality separately plus end-to-end task success.
Prevent permission leaks in every retrieval path and monitor freshness, empty retrievals, latency, cost, and groundedness.

system_design.name: Design a Multi-Model ML Serving Platform
system_design.prompt: Design a multi-tenant platform that serves thousands of ML models for online inference.
clarification_questions: Which model types and hardware are supported?
What latency and availability tiers exist?
How are versions deployed and rolled back?
How bursty is traffic?
What tenant isolation is required?

hidden_constraints.hardware: CPU and GPU pools with expensive cold starts

system_design.exercise: Run a 45-minute mock interview without consulting a solution.
system_design.hermes_connection: Relate local vLLM operation to a heterogeneous fleet without assuming identical constraints.
reference_solution: Separate model registry, deployment control plane, routing, and serving data plane.
Place replicas using resource profiles and SLO tiers; support batching and warm capacity.
Use immutable versions, canaries, shadowing, automated rollback, and reproducible artifacts.
Enforce tenant quotas and admission control to prevent noisy neighbors.
Monitor end-to-end and model-level latency, errors, saturation, quality proxies, skew, and cost.

system_design.name: Design a Coding Agent
system_design.prompt: Design an AI coding agent that can inspect a repository, edit code, run tests, and propose a patch.
clarification_questions: Which repositories and languages are supported?
What actions may the agent take without approval?
How long can a task run?
What success criteria and test signals are available?
How should untrusted repository content be handled?
system_design.exercise: Run a 45-minute mock interview without consulting a solution.
system_design.hermes_connection: Use direct experience with a coding agent to make concrete trade-offs.
reference_solution: Represent each task as a durable state machine around model turns and typed tools.
Build context from repository maps, targeted search, current diffs, test output, and compacted history.
Run file and shell tools in an isolated workspace with network, secret, path, and resource policies.
Checkpoint after tool calls; classify failures and retry only idempotent or explicitly safe actions.
Evaluate patch correctness, test quality, regressions, policy violations, latency, and cost with human review before merge.

system_design.name: Design an Agent Tool Execution Platform
system_design.prompt: Design a platform that lets many AI agents discover and safely execute tools owned by different teams.
clarification_questions: What kinds of tools and side effects are allowed?
How are tools registered and versioned?
How are user and agent permissions represented?
What latency and scale are expected?
How are approvals, retries, and audit logs handled?

hidden_constraints.security: delegated user authority and high-impact mutations

system_design.exercise: Run a 45-minute mock interview without consulting a solution.
system_design.hermes_connection: Use current tool-call permission boundaries as a concrete small-scale example.
reference_solution: Maintain a versioned registry with schemas, ownership, risk class, and idempotency metadata.
Issue short-lived scoped capabilities derived from both user authority and agent policy.
Route calls through validated gateways to isolated executors and controlled egress.
Use call IDs, explicit approval states, deadlines, and tool-specific retry policies.
Capture sanitized inputs, outputs, policy decisions, latency, cost, and side-effect receipts for audit and replay.

system_design.name: Design Memory for a Long-Running Agent
system_design.prompt: Design memory for a personal AI agent that works with a user for years across many tasks.
clarification_questions: What should the agent remember and forget?
Which memory scopes exist?
How should corrections and conflicts be handled?
What privacy and deletion controls are required?
How will memory usefulness be evaluated?

hidden_constraints.quality: incorrect memories are more costly than missing weak signals

system_design.exercise: Run a 45-minute mock interview without consulting a solution.
system_design.hermes_connection: Ground trade-offs in Hermes profile and workflow memory isolation.
reference_solution: Separate immutable event history, task state, user-approved facts, summaries, and ephemeral working memory.
Gate durable writes by confidence, provenance, sensitivity, and user intent.
Retrieve by scope, recency, semantic relevance, and task utility within a fixed context budget.
Keep provenance and versioning so corrections supersede rather than silently erase evidence.
Provide inspect, edit, export, retention, and deletion controls and evaluate both helpful recall and harmful intrusion.

system_design.name: Design a Long-Running Research Agent
system_design.prompt: Design a research agent that can work for hours, browse many sources, recover from failures, and deliver an evidence-backed report.
clarification_questions: What research tasks and sources are supported?
What quality and citation bar is required?
When should the user be consulted?
What time and cost budgets apply?
How should interrupted work resume?

hidden_constraints.recovery: workers may restart at any time
hidden_constraints.quality: every material claim needs traceable evidence

system_design.exercise: Run a 45-minute mock interview without consulting a solution.
system_design.hermes_connection: Relate the design to persistent Hermes tasks and research digests.
reference_solution: Compile the goal into a durable task graph with explicit budgets and completion criteria.
Checkpoint normalized observations, citations, artifacts, and task state after each meaningful step.
Lease work to stateless executors and make retries aware of external side effects.
Use source-quality and contradiction checks before synthesis, preserving claim-to-source provenance.
Pause for human input at ambiguous, costly, sensitive, or irreversible decisions and report partial progress cleanly.

system_design.name: Design Secure Code Execution for Agents
system_design.prompt: Design a secure, multi-tenant code execution sandbox for AI agents running untrusted code.
clarification_questions: Which languages and workloads are supported?
What isolation strength is required?
Is network access allowed?
How are files, secrets, and artifacts handled?
What startup latency and cost targets matter?

hidden_constraints.resources: CPU and GPU pools with strict budgets

system_design.exercise: Run a 45-minute mock interview without consulting a solution.
system_design.hermes_connection: Contrast strong multi-tenant isolation with local development sandboxing.
reference_solution: Use disposable microVM or equivalent strong isolation per execution rather than process-only isolation.
Mount an explicit workspace, inject short-lived scoped secrets, and deny ambient host access.
Default-deny network egress through an audited proxy with destination and protocol policy.
Enforce CPU, memory, disk, process, syscall, time, and output quotas and destroy the environment after capture.
Maintain patched warm pools, signed base images, tamper-resistant audit events, abuse signals, and emergency revocation.
